 By The Philippine Business and News 
 November 20, 2026

 Meralco and the Bulacan Provincial Veterinary Office (PVO) have joined forces to promote responsible pet ownership, humane animal handling and safer communities through a two-day animal welfare initiative in Plaridel, Bulacan.
 Held on October 8 and 9, 2026, the initiative brought together Meralco employees and volunteers, veterinary professionals and residents for humane animal-handling training, community cat management, and free spaying and neutering services.
 The partnership was carried out through Meralco’s animal welfare program CATropa, which seeks to promote responsible and humane care of animals within and beyond company facilities.
 Under the program’s Mission PAW-ssible, the Bulacan PVO trained personnel from Meralco and its subsidiary MIESCOR on the proper handling and humane trapping of community animals found within company facilities.
 MIESCOR personnel return sterilized community cats to their home catios within Meralco’s Plaridel Sector following recovery, as part of the company’s Trap-Neuter-Vaccinate-and-Return program. 
 The training also supports the implementation of Meralco’s Trap-Neuter-Vaccinate-and-Return (TNVR) program at its Plaridel Sector and San Rafael Service Center, with personnel tasked to help manage community cat populations responsibly.
 “Our personnel are often the first to encounter community animals in our facilities, which is why it is important that they know how to handle these situations safely and humanely,” said Mich Caguioa, Head of Advocacy Communication and Meralco CATropa Program Manager.
 “Proper trapping and handling help prevent unnecessary stress and harm to animals while keeping our people safe. Through TNVR and our partnership with the Bulacan Provincial Veterinary Office, we are strengthening our efforts to manage community animal populations responsibly and promote a safer environment for both people and animals,” she added.
 As part of the initiative, Meralco’s Spay It Forward campaign provided free spaying and neutering services to 100 cats and dogs owned by residents of Barangay Agnaya in Plaridel.
 The Bulacan PVO also provided anti-rabies vaccinations and other veterinary services during the medical mission, making essential animal health services more accessible to residents.
 The initiative addresses both animal welfare and public health concerns by promoting responsible animal population management, vaccination and preventive care.
 “We are grateful for partnerships like this that allow us to bring veterinary services closer to communities,” said Dr. Jonathan Ramirez, DVM, Provincial Rabies Program Coordinator.
 “By working together to promote responsible pet ownership, vaccination, and spaying and neutering, we can help manage animal populations humanely and reduce the risk of rabies transmission. These efforts are important not only for animal welfare but also for the safety and well-being of our communities,” he added.
 Following sterilization and recovery, community cats were returned to their home catios within Meralco’s Plaridel Sector as part of the company’s TNVR program.
 The Bulacan Provincial Veterinary Office trains Meralco and MIESCOR personnel on the humane handling and trapping of community animals within company facilities, supporting Meralco CATropa’s TNVR program under Mission PAW-ssible. 
 For Meralco, the initiative reflects its broader approach to community engagement by working with local governments and animal welfare partners on practical programs that benefit both people and animals.
 “Responsible pet ownership and humane animal population management require the collective effort of communities, local governments, and animal welfare advocates,” said Meralco Vice President and Head of Corporate Communications Joe R. Zaldarriaga.
 “Through CATropa, we hope to strengthen these partnerships, make essential veterinary services more accessible, and encourage more communities to take part in protecting both animal welfare and public safety,” he added.
 Since its launch in 2024, Meralco said its animal welfare initiatives have benefited more than 800 cats and dogs within and beyond company properties through humane population management and community-based programs.
 Through CATropa and Spay It Forward, Meralco continues to expand efforts focused on responsible animal care, population management and safer communities.
